data.hypothesis: Keeping the selected parent's 2048-element tile fixed isolates a different finalization strategy: each CTA writes a 64-bit partial, then the last CTA uses a fenced counter to finalize them in the same kernel, replacing the separate partial-reduction kernel. The output counter must be zeroed first on the default stream, so the saved reduction-kernel launch may or may not offset the memset and counter/finalizer work.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this CTA reduction hierarchy, compare finalization strategies while holding the tile size constant; prior measurements show tile-size effects are non-monotonic.
memory_lessons.claim: Measured T2 variants were valid, but performance was non-monotonic with tile size: the 4096-element tile measured 7.3306 μs versus 8.0365 μs for 2048, while 8192 measured 17.6395 μs and 3072 measured 8.1583 μs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this last-CTA finalizer for correctness and three full-program repetitions against the 2048-tile parent; confirm any apparent improvement with additional repetitions.

data.notes: No correctness or timing result is claimed for this candidate. The measured baseline was valid at 46.244 μs mean; the selected 2048-tile parent was valid at 8.0365 μs, and the 4096-tile variant was valid at 7.3306 μs. The CUDA 12.6.3 Programming Guide documents the last-block partial-sum pattern, requiring a fence between partial writes and counter updates and volatile access for visibility: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html (section 7.5). The controller should validate correctness and collect repeated full-program timings; the output serves as a temporary counter for large inputs.
transformations: Keep the 2048-element tile and 128-thread shared-memory CTA reduction, so the changed large-input strategy can be compared with the selected parent without changing grain size.

Replace the separate second reduction kernel with last-CTA finalization: each CTA writes a volatile 64-bit partial, fences before incrementing a per-call output counter, and the last CTA reduces the partials.
Initialize the counter with a default-stream asynchronous memset before the large-input kernel; retain the small-input path, empty sum behavior, bounded tails, and 64-bit intermediate sums.
